summary.intent: Run the full post-execute-phase loop for GSD Phase 66 (API schema cutover / publish gate and tombstone) autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit CLI → ship → resolve PR reviews.
summary.outcome: Completed verify (pre-passed), secure (T-66-E1 write-descriptor escalation found and fixed, SECURITY.md written), SDK E2E gate (green, 5/5 relevant suites), and simplify + CodeRabbit triage (15 findings: 3 fixed, 3 deferred as todos, 9 false positives); transcript ends at the commit stage before validate, ship, and PR steps.

repo: Phase 66 deleted all 5 shares spec files without replacement, leaving zero unit coverage on the reshaped claim/invite paths; the Nyquist validate gate is expected to surface and require this coverage.
89 sdk-e2e tests carry pre-existing `D-01` quarantine skips ('SDK runtime stubbed mid-milestone, re-enable at phase 63-65') on origin/main — not a regression from Phase 66.

Running `pnpm api:generate` runs repo-wide eslint and hits a pre-existing error in `landing/.astro/types.d.ts` (generated/gitignored Astro types) — this error is not blocking and should be ignored during api regeneration.
`api:generate` also reformats `ApiSchemaCutover.ts` (trailing-comma/line-wrap via prettier) even though no migration logic changed — revert migration file after running api:generate.
DTO `@Matches` regex changes do surface into openapi.json but can produce formatting-only churn with no semantic diff; use `jq`-normalized semantic comparison to confirm.
The GSD security enforcement toggle (verify:post hook) was off in config — the secure-phase workflow would have exited early without it, requiring manual audit execution.
The `ipns-publish-gate.test.ts` was the only sdk-e2e file Phase 66 touched; all other suite skips predate the branch.

code.finding: T-66-E1: claim path set Share.writeDescriptorRef from dto.writeDescriptorRef without gating on invite.writeDescriptorRef — a read-only invite could yield a write grant. Fixed by guarding: only propagate dto.writeDescriptorRef when invite.writeDescriptorRef is non-null.
Stale comment (cleaned up). Also: `_publicKey?` param in private `upsertIpnsRecord` method was genuinely unused (single caller, underscore-prefixed), safe to remove.
The new `tombstone` endpoint was missing `@Throttle` decorator while every sibling endpoint (publish, batch, unenroll, resolve) had it. Fixed — destructive endpoints especially need rate limiting.
rootIpnsName used loose `/^k[a-z0-9]+$/` regex; sibling DTOs (resolve, tombstone) use strict `k51qzi5uqu5…|bafzaa…` canonical pattern. Tightened to canonical pattern.
Same loose IPNS regex as create-share.dto — also tightened to canonical pattern for consistency.
UpdateEncryptedKeyDto was a dead export (encrypted-key endpoint removed during phase). Removed from barrel and deleted the source file.
Dead file — only referenced by barrel/generated-dist, no live consumers. Deleted.
CodeRabbit finding #14 (sig bundle partial exposure) was a false positive: controller already fail-closes via `hasSigData = … && result.pubKey`, so a partial/unverifiable bundle is never emitted.

workflow: Security auditor and CodeRabbit CLI independently corroborated T-66-E1 — convergent findings from independent reviewers are a strong signal for real bugs.
CodeRabbit CLI can fail on service connection errors on first attempt; a simple retry resolves it.
CodeRabbit streams findings incrementally — triage only after the process exits (exit 0) to avoid acting on a partial set. Finding count went 3→9→15 in this session.
Re-running the relevant e2e suite (ipns-publish-gate) after each significant code edit is an efficient integration confidence pattern — 5/5 green after every edit confirmed behavior-neutral changes.
Rebuilding the full client chain before restarting the API is required to ensure dist matches the edited source; skipping it produces stale behavior in e2e.
When `api:generate` produces a semantically-empty openapi.json diff, revert it before committing to avoid noisy diffs and potential pre-commit hook churn.
The commit helper can report `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — verify with `git log --oneline -1`.
